rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scriptural People of the Book do not develop deliberate, cultivated doubt because their knowledge already matches the truth of the number.
rows.anchor: أي يشك شكا يحصل بتعمد وتكسب

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Burjān reports from Jābir that some People of the Book asked the Prophet about Hell’s keepers; he indicated ten, then nine, and they affirmed him. Asked about Paradise’s keepers, they answered, “a loaf.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن برجان : وروى جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers whose faith is firmly rooted do not doubt because the proofs have made the matter as clear to them as daylight.
rows.anchor: لا يرتاب الذين رسخ الإيمان عندهم لما رأوا من الدلائل التي جعلتهم في مثل ضوء النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart’s illness means doubt or even a small measure of hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: أي شك أو نفاق وإن قل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra’s prediction of people with hypocrisy before hypocrites existed is a sign of prophethood.
rows.anchor: ونزول هذه السورة قبل وجود المنافقين علم من أعلام النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may intend one result as His primary purpose and arrange another as a secondary purpose; leaving a town to oppose most people illustrates the distinction.
rows.anchor: ولا ينكر جعل الله تعالى بعض الأمور مقصودة لشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are people settled in disbelief, certain and open in their denial, who conceal the truth shown by the proofs.
rows.anchor: أي ويقول الراسخون في الكفر الجازمون بالتكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible sense of “a likeness” is something so startling that the small number seems astonishing beside God’s greatness.
rows.anchor: من جهة أنه صار بذلك مستغربا استغراب المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “likeness” signals that the number is not meant literally but represents something they failed to understand.
rows.anchor: أو أن ذلك إشارة إلى أنه ليس المراد به ظاهره بل مثل لشيء لم يفهموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They wrongly take the small count to conflict with divine majesty; few in number can be stronger than many and better demonstrate comprehensive power.
rows.anchor: وما علموا أن القليل من حيث العدد قد يكون أعظم

words: كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides or misguides whomever He wills, through whatever words He wills, by this very statement or by another means.
rows.anchor: أي الذي له مجامع العظمة ومعاقد العز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deliberately obscure count of nineteen tests temperaments: the deviant demand an explanation, then reject or doubt what they cannot fathom, while the sound-natured submit and affirm that all is from their Lord.
rows.anchor: لأن المنحرف الطباع يبحث عن عللها بحثا متعنتا

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows the number and qualities of His troops, including the keepers of Hell; their count says nothing about the limit of His forces.
rows.anchor: أي المحسن إليك بأنواع الإحسان المدبر لأمرك

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says seventy thousand angels enter the Frequented House each day and never return for another turn.
rows.anchor: فقد روي أن البيت المعمور يدخله كل يوم سبعون ألفا من الملائكة لا تعود إليهم نوبة أخرى

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report compares the earth within heaven to a ring cast in a desert, and each heaven to the one above it in the same way.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد أن الأرض في السماء كحلقة ملقاة في فلاة وكل سماء في التي فوقها كذلك

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says heaven groans, as it should, because every space the size of a foot contains a standing angel at prayer.
rows.anchor: ورد في الخبر : أطت السماء وحق لها أن تئط

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels once included those who uprooted the seven towns of Lot’s people and lifted them to the sky.
rows.anchor: فقد كان في الملائكة من اقتلع مدائن قوم لوط وهي سبع ورفعها إلى عنان السماء

words: وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every substance and accident in a human is among God’s troops: disrupting a still vein, stopping a moving one, or blocking or opening a cavity could kill a person.
rows.anchor: لو تحرك عرق ساكن أو سكن متحرك أو انسد مجوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hellfire is a powerful reminder for all people; embodied humans already know its effects, though God can create something more painful and severe than anything creatures know.
rows.anchor: أي تذكرة عظيمة لكل من هو ظاهر البشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obscure description of God’s forces mercifully opens a path to surrender to divine wisdom; emphasis suits most hearers’ crooked temperaments and tendency to reject.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك من رحمة العباد ليفتح لهم بابا إلى التسليم لما يغمض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He begins with the cold moon to signal the coming heat, glare, breathlessness, and despair; the heavenly signs are especially fearsome.
rows.anchor: ذكرها بادئا بما طبعه البرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God erases the moon’s appearance as in an earthly eclipse, but without a physical cause, as causal regularity ends and wonders appear.
rows.anchor: أذهب صورته كما تذهب صورة الأرض المخسوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are brought together with overwhelming force and ease; their light is useless, yet their forms remain perceptible because hidden things are fully disclosed.
rows.anchor: أي جمعا هو في غاية الإحكام ولاشدة كما أفهمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive verb foregrounds the terrifying union that overturns normal order and also conveys how effortlessly it occurs.
rows.anchor: وبني الفعل للمفعول لأن المهول مطلق جمعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After being joined, the sun and moon are cast into the Fire like two slaughtered bulls.
rows.anchor: وبعد جمعها يلقيان في النار كأنهما ثوران عقيران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human asks where to flee in panic and bewilderment, driven by instinct amid the supreme calamity; Hell is then dragged by seventy thousand chains, each held by seventy thousand angels.
rows.anchor: أي بشدة روعه جريا مع طبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No refuge” means there is no shelter, protector, fortress, or place of escape.
rows.anchor: أي ملجأ ومعتصم ولا حصن ولا التجاء واعتصام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person’s own recognition that escape is impossible after first asking the question makes the scene’s terror more vivid.
rows.anchor: فقال معبرا بالأداة الجامعة لمجامع الردع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creation—speaking and silent, its place and time of rest—ultimately lies under God’s judgment and will, outwardly and inwardly; none other rules it.
rows.anchor: استقرار الخلق كلهم ناطقهم وصامتهم ومكان قرارهم وزمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At judgment a person tries to excuse every evil deed, speaking quickly to seem sincere, eager, and ingratiating, but the speech itself testifies against him.
rows.anchor: أي ذكر بغاية السرعة ذلك الإنسان من غير تلعثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word can mean excuses or room to maneuver; al-Qāmūs also gives “screens” and “arguments,” linked because both cover a sinner or sin.
rows.anchor: المعاذير : الستور والحجج جمع معذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excuses fail because the person was given insight but blinded it through the humiliation of the self and its appetites; the innate light of knowledge remains evidence against him.
rows.anchor: لأنه قد أعطى البصيرة فأعماها بهون النفس وشهواتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike ordinary people, the Prophet was created complete, continually advanced in perfection, and was not distracted from knowledge; his perception reached beyond ordinary limits.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مبرءا من ذلك لخلق الله له كاملا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that his companions’ humility and bowing were not hidden from him because he could see them from behind his back.
rows.anchor: والله لا يخفى علي خشوعكم ولا ركوعكم أني أراكم من وراء ظهري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also says the Prophet could see in the darkest conditions and had an unmatched delicacy of constitution and complete unveiling.
rows.anchor: وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يرى في أشد الظلام وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Prophet received the Qur’an with exceptional perception, Gabriel’s delivery caused him strain; out of reverence and fear of forgetting, he hurriedly moved his tongue to secure every word.
rows.anchor: ولأنه كلام الملك الأعظم , وبأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command corrects the Prophet’s haste and announces that God removed the veils that ordinarily hide realities, showing the Qur’an is divinely given rather than the Prophet’s own composition.
rows.anchor: قد دفع عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تلك الحجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s action is governed by God’s will, as stated in the cited verse; the revelation came by divine choice, not the Prophet’s acquisition.
rows.anchor: لأنه ما نزله إليه بغير اكتساب منه إلا وقد شاء ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s tongue has no movement except in remembering God.
rows.anchor: الذي ليست له حركة إلا في ذكر الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He hurried to receive and retain the Qur’an before Gabriel finished delivering it, fearing that a word might slip from memory.
rows.anchor: أي بحمله وأخذه قبل أن يفرغ من إلقاءه إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This haste was praiseworthy because love of God and His message motivated it, yet it was a lower station than perfect calm reception; the Prophet was moved from a good state to a better one.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا حامل له عليه إلا حب الله وحب ما يأتي منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ haste to please God is a parallel example of eagerness in obedience, though the Qur’anic context marks a still more complete state for Muhammad.
rows.anchor: كما قال موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These Qur’an-related verses distinguish the self-reproach that urges good from self-reproach in wrongdoing, and return to the accusation that the Qur’an is human speech; the resurrection passage was an intervening excursus.
rows.anchor: والآية ناظرة غلى قوله تعالى في المدثر حكاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Gabriel recites, the Prophet should listen intently, attend with his mind, repeat the passage until fluent, and practice it until it becomes a character that leads to good.
rows.anchor: أي بغاية جهدك بإلقاء سمعك وإحضار ذهنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the Qur’an, meaning Gabriel’s recitation of it, or to Gabriel himself, meaning follow his reading without addressing him.
rows.anchor: فالضمير يجوز أن يكون للقرآن أي قراءة جبريل عليه السلام له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then” signals a delay suited to the greatness of explaining the Qur’an and permits explanation after the initial address, when it is needed; the Prophet may also have hurried to ask about its meaning.
rows.anchor: دالا على جواز تأخير البيان عن وقت الخطاب إلى وقت الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guarantees explanation of the Qur’an’s words, arrangement, and meanings, whether Gabriel’s delivery sounds like a bell or ordinary speech; its explanation reaches others through the Prophet and the umma’s scholars.
rows.anchor: أي بيان ألفاظه ومعانيه لك سواء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Through Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ibn ʿAbbās reports that revelation strained the Prophet, who moved his lips; God revealed these instructions, after which he listened silently to Gabriel and recited the passage when Gabriel left. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : ( كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faces expect disaster from the visible signs; “face” stands for the whole person, and the passive wording focuses on the harm rather than its agent.
rows.anchor: أي تتوقع بما ترى من المخايل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine “her” refers to people: if the noblest part, the face, is struck, the rest of the person is even more exposed to harm.
rows.anchor: أي بهم فإنه إذا أصيب الوجه الذي هو أشرف ما في الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fāqira is a calamity that breaks the vertebrae, the strongest bones, and thus breaks one’s back.
rows.anchor: أي داهية تكسر الفقاره وهو عظم سلسلة الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses interwoven omission: the first group’s mention of looking signals its opposite for the second group, while the second group’s calamity signals its opposite for the first.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر النظر في الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke means that love of the immediate world cannot continue: it will be violently broken at the terror of death.
rows.anchor: أي لا يدوم هذا الحب بل لا بد أن ينقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unspoken subject of “reaches” is the soul, inferred because it is the one that loves the present world.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المحب للدنيا هو النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tarāqī are the upper chest bones around the throat on both sides, between the hollow of the neck and the shoulder; their arrival marks death’s choking onset.
rows.anchor: أي عظام أعالي الصدر , جمع ترقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using a plural for the pair may suggest the soul’s desperate movement from the body’s farthest parts into a narrowing space, seeking the nearest exit.
rows.anchor: لعله جمع المثنى إشارة إلى شدة انتشارها بغاية الجهد

rows.speaker: حاتم الطائي
rows.claim: Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī’s verse says wealth cannot help when the dying person chokes and the chest tightens, illustrating the death scene.
rows.anchor: قول حاتم الطائي وأشد التئامه مع ما هنا من أمر الروح : أماوي ما يغني الثراء عن الفتى إذا حشرجت يوما وضاق بها الصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person’s family are distressed and call out for someone to save him, but no particular speaker is identified, so the statement is passive.
rows.anchor: كان قولهم كأنه لا قائل له على التعيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordinary question asks who has the established skill in healing incantations to rescue the dying person, beyond the reach of medicine.
rows.anchor: أي من هو الذي يتصف برسوخ القدم في أمر الرقى الشافية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says angels ask which will take the soul upward: the angels of mercy or the angels of punishment.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن هذا القول من بعض الملائكة للاستفهام عمن يرقى بروحه إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word can derive from raqā meaning to perform an incantation, or from raqā meaning to ascend; the latter reading concerns the soul’s ascent.
rows.anchor: فالأول اسم فاعل من رقى يرقى بمعنى الرقية بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person—or a relative asking who can help—anticipates the final separation; it is called a supposition because people waver and cling to familiar things at the slightest cue.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإنسان مطبوعا على الترجح بين الأمور الممكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes the dying person’s joints greeting one another: “Peace; you part from me, and I from you, until Resurrection.” No attribution or grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ففي الخبر أن العبد ليعالج كرب الموت وسكراته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The legs close around one another like a single thing; this depicts death, since walking requires alternating legs except in extreme circumstances such as battle.
rows.anchor: أي انضمت إليها واتصلت بها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the phrase as the joining of the final hardship of this world with the first hardship of the next.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه كناية عن اختلاط شدة آخر الدنيا بشدة أول الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted consequence is that the dying person’s attachment to the world, love of it, and aversion to the next life come to an end.
rows.anchor: وجواب إذ محذوف تقديره : زال تعلقه الذي كان بالدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-masāq means the driving, its destination, and its time; all fall under the rule of the Lord who sent and supported the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أي السوق وموضع السوق وزمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After death angels drive each person toward clear happiness or misery; alternatively, the phrase means presentation before God, where “I will die and rest” cannot help the sinner, who is received like an absconding slave according to his disobedience.
rows.anchor: فإما أن تسوقه الملائكة إلى سعادة بينة وإما إلى شقاوة بينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person neither believed the Messenger’s warning about evil deeds nor affirmed the call to spend on good works; the omitted object broadens the denial to all such deeds, and the passage answers the rejection of resurrection in 75:6.
rows.anchor: القيامة : 6 ] الذي معناه جحد البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He did none of the prescribed prayer, obligatory or voluntary, severing both his bond with the Creator and, as law directs, his bond with other people; even disbelievers are addressed by subsidiary duties.
rows.anchor: أي ما أمر به من فرض وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instead he actively denied God’s message and turned away from prayer and obedience, persisting until his original sound nature died and his commanding self prevailed; this is not redundant because lack of affirmation is not itself denial.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا بتكرار لأنه لا يلزم من عدم التصديق التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier goes home unconcerned with the consequences and flaunts his rejection; indulgence corrupted his practical and intellectual faculties until indifference became an ingrained vice he boasts about.
rows.anchor: أي هذا الإنسان بعد توليه عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatamaṭṭā means swaggering in pride; it is linked either to stretching the back and stride or to twisting the back while strutting, instead of showing shame and humility.
rows.anchor: أي يفتخر افتخارا بتكذيبه وإعراضه وعدم مبالاته بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This threat is the fitting reply in place of his family’s greeting: may God bring what he hates and strike him with one calamity after another.
rows.anchor: أي أولاك الله ما تكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām emphasizes the threat, its repetition across the two verses signals the enormity and enduring desert of the offense, and the successive calamities may be immediate or delayed and vary in severity.
rows.anchor: وأبلغ ذلك التأكيد إشارة إلى أنه يستحقه على مدى الأعصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase urges him to leave his present conduct and turn to what benefits him.
rows.anchor: أن تترك ما أنت عليه وتقبل على ما ينفعك

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports that after Abū Jahl mocked the nineteen keepers of Hell, God told the Prophet to meet him in Mecca and say these words to him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جرير في تفسير المدثر : إن أبا جهل لما استهزأ
